title: Isolation and culture of neural stem cells from adult mouse subventricular zone for genetic and pharmacological treatments with proliferation analysis
protocol: Fill the syringe with tamoxifen and wipe the tip of the syringe before inserting the needle on the syringe.
Perform i.p. injection with 250 μl (5 mg) of 20 mg/ml Tamoxifen per mouse, 3 days before the NSC harvest.
Clean gross dissection tools with 70% ethanol and allow to air dry.
Immerse tissue slicer blades, a mouse coronal acrylic matrix, and forceps in a beaker containing 70% ethanol with lint-free tissue paper lining the bottom.
Place the beaker on ice to cool down the instruments.
Rinse the tools in ice-cold RPMI media before touching brain tissue with them.
Prepare Dissection Media and chill it to 4°C.
Prepare 200 mL of dissection media for washing tools and an additional 25 mL for the SVZ pooled from 2 mouse brains.
Place 22 mL of dissection media into a 100 mm cell culture plate.
Place 3 mL of dissection media into a 35 mm cell culture plate for each pair of mice.
Prepare NSC proliferation media on the day of dissection.
Make a midline incision through the bone on the dorsal side of skull from the cut surface at the base of the skull to the orbits using a small scissor (2 cm blade).
Remove the brain from the skull using a flat tip forcep and place it in the coronal acrylic brain matrice with the dorsal surface of the brain facing up.
Place blades, 1 mm apart, in the matrix starting from the brain-olfactory bulb interface to the rostral end of the dorsal hippocampus.
Keep blades and matrix cold and moist by storing them in ice-cold RPMI and on ice respectively.
Transfer each brain slice from the blade to the chilled dissection media using a pre-cooled flat tip forcep.
Collect all brain slices up to the dorsal hippocampus, discarding sections beyond this region.
Identify brain slices where lateral ventricles are separated from each other under a dissecting microscope.
Dissect the SVZ from the brain slices using fine tip forceps and angled spring scissors.
Incise a 1–2 mm wide layer of tissue bordering the lateral ventricles including the ventral apex, medial wall, and lateral wall of the ventricle in each slice.
Identify the striatum by its speckled appearance under the microscope.
Dissect the tissue between the striatum and the lateral ventricle for the SVZ.
Place the dissected SVZ in chilled dissection media in a 35 mm dish kept on ice.
Mince the dissected SVZ tissue into pieces less than 1 mm thick.
Pin the tissue with a #11 scalpel blade tip and use forceps to pull the tissue towards the sharp edge of the scalpel for mincing.
Collect minced SVZ tissue in 50 mL conical tubes using a regular p1000 pipette tip.
Wash the bottom of each 35 mm plate with the last 1 mL of dissection media to dislodge remaining pieces of SVZ tissue.
Spin the tissue at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the tissue in 1 mL pre-warmed 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA at 37°C.
Incubate the tissue in a 37°C water bath for 5 min.
Add an equal volume (1 mL) of 1 mg/mL Trypsin Inhibitor solution to the tissue.
Use a 3 mL syringe with a 25G needle to dissociate the tissue into cells, taking care not to introduce air bubbles during trituration.
Spin the cells at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and gently resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL NSC Proliferation Media.
Transfer the cells to a deep 100 mm plate with NSC Proliferation Media (total 20 mL).
Incubate the cells at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Allow dissociated cells to expand for 48 h without disruption.
Add fresh 40 μL of 10 μg/mL EGF (final concentration 20 ng/mL) directly to each dish.
Add fresh 20 μL of 10 μg/mL bFGF (final concentration 10 ng/mL) directly to each dish.
Add fresh 20 μL of 0.2% Heparin (final concentration 0.0002%) directly to each dish.
Swirl the dishes gently after adding growth factors and heparin.
Allow primary neurospheres to grow for 7 days or until they reach an average diameter of 150 μm.
Warm NSC Proliferation media to room temperature.
Add growth factor supplements to an aliquot of NSC Proliferation media.
Warm 0.25% Trypsin and 1 mg/mL Trypsin Inhibitor in a 37°C dry/water bath.
Remove plates with neurospheres from the incubator.
Collect 10 ml of media with neurospheres in a 50 ml conical tube using a sterile 10 ml serological pipet.
Dislodge attached neurospheres by gently pipetting remaining 10 ml of media in the plate, repeatedly ∼2–3 times.
Add the remaining 10 mL of media containing dislodged neurospheres to the previous 10 mL media in a 50 mL conical tube.
Spin the neurospheres at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and add 1 mL Trypsin to the pellet followed by needle trituration.
Incubate the dissociated neurospheres in a 37°C dry/water bath for up to 5 min.
Add an equal volume (1 mL) of 1 mg/mL Trypsin inhibitor and swirl gently to mix.
Dissociate the neurospheres into a single cell suspension by needle trituration using a 3 mL syringe with a 25G needle.
Spin the cells at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL NSC Proliferation media.
Plate cells in 20 mL of NSC Proliferation media in a deep 100 mm plate.
Passage neurospheres when they reach 150 μm diameter.
Etch the glass coverslips for 6 h by immersing them in 1 M hydrochloric acid at 37°C.
Rinse the coverslips twice in 70% ethanol at room temperature.
Incubate coverslips in 70% ethanol for 6-12 hours at 120-200 rpm on a shaker at room temperature.
Dry coverslips by placing them at a 45° angle in the wells of a 24-well plate for at least 12 hours or overnight.

Coat wells of 24-well plates directly with Growth Factor Reduced Matrigel (GFR-Matrigel) for total RNA extraction, or coat etched coverslips for immunofluorescent analysis the day before NSC dissociation.
Thaw GFR-Matrigel on ice.
Mix 1 mg of GFR-Matrigel with 12 mL of cold media (RPMI, DMEM, or any buffered media).
Add 500 μL of GFR-Matrigel/media mixture to each well using a pre-chilled micropipette tip.
Shake the plate to ensure the media covers the entire coverslip/well.
Place plates in a biosafety cabinet for 3-12 hours at room temperature to allow the GFR-Matrigel to polymerize.
Store plates containing GFR-Matrigel at 37°C for up to 2 weeks.
Aspirate the GFR-Matrigel from the wells immediately before plating the cells.
Dissociate proliferating neurospheres as described in steps 17–22.
Incubate the neurospheres in 0.25% Trypsin at 37°C for up to 5 minutes.
Add an equal volume of trypsin inhibitor to inactivate the trypsin.
Dissociate the neurospheres into a single cell suspension by needle trituration using a 3 mL syringe and 25G needle.
Spin the dissociated cells at 500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend NSCs in 1 mL NSC Proliferation media by pipetting the pellet approximately 3 times.
Dilute cells to obtain 12 mL cell suspension with 1.5 × 10^6 cells in NSC Proliferation media.
Mix 3 × 10^6 cells with plasmid DNA for nucleoporation using the Amaxa Nucleofector 2b machine and Mouse NSC Nucleofector kit.
Add 0.5 mL of nucleofector supplement to 2.25 mL of Cell Line Nucleofector Solution V to prepare the Mouse Neural Stem Cell Nucleofector Solution.
Combine media components to room temperature before use, including Mouse Neural Stem Cell (NSC) Nucleofector Solution and NSC Proliferation Media.
Thaw plasmids of interest without warming them to room temperature.
Determine the cell number to obtain 3 × 10^6 total cells for a 24-well plate (1.25 × 10^5 cells/well).
Pellet the cells by centrifuging at 150×g for 5 min at 4°C.
Prepare Mouse NSC Nucleofector Solution with the necessary plasmid mixtures in a separate microfuge tube.
Add 100 μL of Mouse NSC Nucleofector Solution to the tube containing cells.
For nucleofection of 3 × 10^6 cells, add 10 μg of plasmid to the Mouse NSC Nucleofector Solution.
Mix by pipetting.
Turn on the machine and set the Amaxa Nucleofector Program to A-33 or A-033.
Aspirate the supernatant from pelleted cells.

Resuspend the cell pellet with 100 μL of Plasmid + Mouse NSC Nucleofector solution using a p200 pipette with a filter tip by gently pipetting 3–5 times or until the cells are resuspended in a homogenous opaque solution.
Transfer the cell mixture from the microfuge tube to the bottom of a cuvette.
Place the cuvette in the Amaxa Nucleofector machine and run program A-33 or A-033.
Immediately add 500 μL of NSC Proliferation Solution at room temperature to the cell mixture.
Transfer the cells from the cuvette back to the microfuge tube used to pellet the cells.
For 3 × 10^6 cells, add 600 μL nucleofected cell solution to 11.4 mL of NSC Proliferation Media and mix gently by pipetting.
Plate 500 μl of the mixed cell suspension in each well of a 24-well plate.
For 1.5 × 10^6 cells, resuspend nucleofected cells in 5.4 ml of NSC Proliferation Media and plate 500 μl per well for total 12 wells.
Allow cells to adhere overnight (8–16 h) before changing the media to NSC Differentiation media.
Treat the cells with GANT58 or DMSO 3–4 h after plating when >90% of cells have attached to the matrigel coated wells.
Dilute 12 μL of 50 mM GANT58 (or DMSO) in 1.2 mL NSC Differentiation Media for accurate pipetting.
Add 50 μL diluted GANT58 or vehicle to 450 μL NSC Differentiation media per well and gently swirl the plate to mix.
Return treated plates to the incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Change the media completely with fresh NSC Differentiation media every 48 h for up to 14 days.
Wash the cells twice with sterile HBSS or PBS.
Add 250 μL of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA to each well of a 24-well plate.
Incubate for 5–6 min at room temperature or until the cells begin to lift.
Inactivate trypsin by adding an equal volume of 1 mg/mL Trypsin Inhibitor solution to each well.
Transfer cells from every 3 wells into a 2 mL microfuge tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 500g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 50 μL of Monarch DNA/RNA Protection Reagent.
Store the resuspended cells at −80°C until RNA extraction.
Prepare EdU stock solution by dissolving 50 mg EdU in 9.9 mL DMSO to make a 20 mM stock solution.
Dilute the 20 mM EdU stock solution to 20 μM in NSC differentiation media.
Mix 12 μL of 20 mM EdU stock with 1.2 mL NSC differentiation media to make a 20 μM EdU working solution.
Add 50 μL of 20 μM EdU working solution to the cells in each well of a 24-well plate.
Incubate for 1 h.
Pre-chill methanol (MeOH) to −20°C before beginning wash and fixation steps.
Aspirate all media from each well.
Wash with 500 μL of 1× PBS.
Aspirate the PBS from the wells.
Add 500 μL of chilled MeOH to each well.
Incubate the plates at room temperature for 10–15 min.
Aspirate the methanol from each well.
Wash each well with 1× PBS for 3–5 min.
Repeat the washes 3 times.
Prepare fresh blocking solution consisting of 10% serum in immunofluorescent labeling buffer solution.
Incubate the cells with blocking solution for 1 hour at room temperature.
Aspirate the blocking solution.
Dilute primary antibodies in the immunofluorescent labeling buffer solution.
Incubate the cells with primary antibodies for 3 hours at room temperature.
Wash the cells 3 times with 1× PBS for 5 minutes per wash.
Dilute secondary antibodies and Hoechst in the immunofluorescent labeling buffer solution.
Add the diluted secondary antibody + Hoechst solution to the cells.
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash coverslips 3 times with PBS for 5 minutes per wash.
Put 4 drops of Fluoromount-G onto a standard microscope slide.
Aspirate the PBS from the coverslips.
Slowly invert each coverslip on a drop of Fluoromount-G.
Allow the Fluoromount-G to solidify overnight (12 h minimum) at room temperature before imaging.
